name_note: GTDB splits classical Haemophilus influenzae into several species; the genomes it places in s__Haemophilus influenzae_E are named Haemophilus influenzae in NCBI, so this taxon is narrower than H. influenzae as used in papers.

sentences.text: Nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae is described as a commensal microbe often isolated from the upper and lower respiratory tract that can cause sinusitis and acute otitis media in preschool children.
Nontypeable H. influenzae and Streptococcus pneumoniae have been described as pathobionts sharing niches in the upper respiratory tract, which can form part of the resident upper airway microbiota.
In nasopharyngeal swabs from 6420 healthy French children aged 6 months to 15 years, H. influenzae carriage mirrored pneumococcal patterns in early childhood but declined with age.
That study also reported that co-carriage of pneumococcus with H. influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis was frequent, independent of age.
